findings.title: Layers, thickness and copper weight
findings.message: The board has 4 copper layers. PCBWay's standard price is for 2 layers; 4 layers cost extra and may not be covered by the sponsored round.
findings.fix: Ask the course staff before ordering more than 2 layers, or move the design to 2 layers.

checks.title: Power track width for the rated current
Vias where the power path changes layer

findings.title: Vias where the power path changes layer
findings.message: /48V_BUS: the power path changes layer through 1 via(s), good for about 0.7 A, but this net carries ~3.5 A.
findings.fix: Use at least 8 vias of 0.3 mm (or fewer 0.4 mm ones), placed across the current flow, or keep the power path on one layer.

locations.label: via 0.4 mm

findings.title: Input/output connectors
findings.message: No polarity/voltage label found on the silkscreen next to J2. Swapped input wires destroy the board.
findings.fix: Add silkscreen text such as 'VIN 20-48V +  -' / '12V OUT +  -' next to each pin.

locations.label: J2

findings.title: Input/output connectors
findings.message: U4 (LM358) carries ~5.0 A on GND through 1 pin(s) at 2.54 mm pitch. Connectors with 2.54 mm pitch or less (pin headers, JST) are rated about 1-3 A per pin.
findings.fix: Use a 5.08 mm screw terminal, banana jacks or XT30/XT60, or put several pins in parallel.

locations.label: U4

findings.fix: Use a 5.08 mm screw terminal, banana jacks or XT30/XT60, or put several pins in parallel.

findings.title: Capacitor voltage ratings
findings.message: Voltage rating unknown for 1 power capacitor(s): C2. Check them by hand: input side >= 63 V, output side >= 16 V.
findings.fix: Put the rating in the value (e.g. '100uF 63V') or in a 'Voltage' field so the checker can read it.

checks.title: Hot loop: input capacitor at the switches

findings.title: Hot loop: input capacitor at the switches
findings.message: No ceramic capacitor found between the input and ground. Electrolytic caps alone cannot supply the fast switching current; the switch node will ring.
findings.fix: Put 1-3 ceramic capacitors (e.g. 2.2-10 µF 100 V X7R) right at the switches, across input and ground.

checks.title: Gate driver close to the MOSFETs

findings.title: Gate driver close to the MOSFETs
findings.message: U3 pin 3 is 20 mm from the gate of Q2. A long gate loop slows switching and picks up noise.
findings.fix: Move the driver within about 15 mm of the MOSFET, and run the gate and its return (source) side by side.

locations.label: Q2 gate

findings.title: Gate driver close to the MOSFETs
findings.message: The gate drive tracks of Q2 (Net-(D4-A), Net-(U3-HO)) are 39 mm long in total.
findings.fix: Keep the gate drive under about 30 mm.

locations.label: Q2

findings.title: Test points (EE463: verify supplies and gate signals)
findings.message: The board has no test points. EE463 asks you to check the auxiliary supplies and gate signals before powering the power stage.
findings.fix: Add test points (or a small header) for ground, each auxiliary supply, each gate signal and the switch node.

findings.title: Test points (EE463: verify supplies and gate signals)
findings.message: No test point on ground. Every probe needs a ground point nearby.
findings.fix: Add one or two GND test points (a loop or hook type is easiest for scope probes).

findings.title: Test points (EE463: verify supplies and gate signals)
findings.message: No test point on the gate signal of Q2 (Net-(D4-A) / Net-(U3-HO)).
findings.fix: Add a test point on the gate (or the driver output) so you can see the gate waveform.
